subject: DevAdvocacy LiveHack — credits governance and segmented allocation
body:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Samira Blaine <samira@livingsketch.io>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DevAdvocacy LiveHack — credits governance and segmented allocation

Hi team,

We need a quick sign-off on the promo/credit plan for the LivingSketch LiveHack (Sept 9). Samira asked for a pool of trial credits to distribute to attendees and a small reserve for speakers/community leads. I sketched a conservative split in the attached spreadsheet (livehack-credit-split-v1.xlsx) — summary below: 

- Total pool requested: 400 trial credits (equivalent to ~200k tokens at our standard conversion)
  - Attendee distribution: 260 codes (auto-redeemable, 90-day window)
  - Speaker & volunteer extras: 100 codes (manual assignment)
  - Ops/reserve: 40 codes (for refunds/late adds)

Operational asks: 
- Per-account cap: enforce 1 code per HubSpot contact; redeemable once.
- Max value per code: $250 equivalent (we should translate to token budget).
- Tracking: Samira needs a redemption report and a tracking link back to HubSpot campaign "LS-LiveHack-2026".
- Legal: attach trial terms (redwood_trial_terms.pdf) for partner sign-off.

Samira, can LivingSketch guarantee the attendee list will be collected via the registration form (we'll link codes to emails to prevent mass sharing)?

Please reply with any objections or edits; if nobody objects by 1:00pm PT I will approve the pool and ask Ops to mint the codes and hand them to Samira next week.

Thanks,
Irene
--
Irene Choi
Director, Developer Advocacy
Redwood Inference


On Tue, 11 Aug 2026 at 10:03 AM, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
> To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
> Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 10:03:00 -0700
> Subject: Re: DevAdvocacy LiveHack — credits governance and segmented allocation
>
> Thanks for the clear breakdown, Irene. A couple of operational suggestions:
>
> - Set the per-account cap as both: 1 code per email and a token ceiling equivalent to $200 to limit unexpected spend.
> - Make the speaker extras 80 codes and move 20 into ops reserve — we should avoid manual authorizations unless necessary.
> - Require the HubSpot campaign ID on every redemption so Marketing can reconcile.
>
> If Accounting is comfortable with the total pool (400), I’m fine approving. Otherwise, reduce total to 350 and keep attendee allocation high.
>
> -Marcus
>
>--
>Marcus Lin
>Head of Growth, Redwood Inference
>

>
> Quick note from Partnerships: Samira asked us to reserve a small "community lead" bundle of codes (about 30) to give to organizers at universities and partner meetups. Those are used to seed higher-quality community discussions.
>
> So my proposed adjusted split:
> - Attendees: 250
> - Speaker extras: 90
> - Community lead bundle: 30
> - Ops reserve: 30
>
> Also, we should issue speaker extras as single-use codes tied to speaker emails (helps with attribution). Samira, will you provide a list of speaker emails by Aug 26?
>
>Vanessa
>
>--
>Vanessa Ortiz
>Partnerships, Redwood Inference

> I'm okay with the split Vanessa suggested. A couple asks from the sales/sponsor side:
>
> - Can we convert 10 of the ops reserve to sponsor co-branded codes (these will be gift codes we can use in follow-up demos)?
> - Please confirm redemption window is 90 days and that codes expire automatically.
>
> If we can reserve the 10 sponsor codes, I approve the rest and will drop a HubSpot task to Samira for speaker emails.
>
>Karthik
>Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
